source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting structural defects in a bridge maintenance report

1. Start with the maintenance records.
2.
completion:
Scan the bridge visually. Begin at one end and work your way through the bridge, examining top decks, abutments/pier caps, abutments/piers, and foundations.
3. Use photos! Photos can document many conditions and provide a visual reference. They can be used to create detailed bridge logs in the future. Be sure they are dated and numbered.
4. Look for exfiltration or infiltration around the spandrel walls and deck seams. Use a probe to check for weakness or deterioration of the guardrail posts. Probes can be made from old tool handles or similar materials.
5. As you work your way through the bridge, note, while standing above the deck, water discoloration on nearby abutments/piers that may indicate water issues originating on the structure above.
6. Test spalling or scaling in the deck and under bridge surfaces. Use a pointed instrument, scraper or probe.
7. Sound deck surfaces
